title: EPP0129 - Bedding Plants
description:
Essex County Council, through the Essex Procurement Partnership, is procuring Bedding Plants on behalf of Tendring District Council.\r
\r
Tendring District Council ("the Council") places much emphasis on the quality of the environment within the District for the benefit of residents and visitors and the provision of high class and colourful bedding plant displays throughout its public gardens form a major part of current grounds maintenance programme.\r
\r
The Council uses a wide range of seasonal bedding plants in public gardens across the District, the main displays are located at Clacton Seafront, Crescent Gardens Frinton, Marine Gardens Walton and Mayors Garden Dovercourt. There are further smaller displays at other locations.\r
\r
Planting typically commences during the 1st week of June for Summer Bedding and the\r
1st week of October for Spring Bedding and is undertaken over three to four week periods. The Council's Open Spaces team carry out planting and maintenance across the District.\r
\r
Plants for spring bedding will be ordered by the end of May and plants for summer bedding will be ordered by the last week in October in each cyclic period. The Contractor will be advised of the exact planting dates for each planting period approximately one month before delivery, this will be dependent on growing conditions and how the current seasonal displays look.\r
\r
The contractor will be required to deliver all plants to nominated points throughout the District and timeliness of delivery is crucial. On average the Council orders approximately 45,000 to 67,500 plants per year for its displays approximately 40,000 to 60,000 for the summer period and 5,000 to 7,500 plants for the autumn period.\r
\r
The Council may order any combination of plants during the contract period for its bedding scheme The Council may place orders with the Supplier based upon a production list of plant requirements chosen from the Pricing Schedule, The pricing rate that shall be applied for each variety of each species will be determined by the total requirement for that variety contained within the individual order.\r
\r
For information there are no assets available for use on this contract. \r

title: Economic and Employment Study Tender
description:
Tendring District Council and Colchester Borough Council in partnership with Essex County Council (the Councils) seek to appoint consultants to undertake an Economic and Employment Study to inform the preparation of the emerging Tendring Colchester Borders Garden Community Development Plan Document (DPD). The study will:
•	advise the Councils of the potential means of maximising the positive economic and employment generation opportunities of the Garden Community development
•	include analysis and options for location, format and potential end-users of the 25 hectares of employment allocation envisaged as part of the development
•	take into account the long-term nature of the development and the potential for innovation and change over the period of construction

title: EPP0014 - Active Outdoor Gym
description:
Essex County Council are procuring on behalf of Tendring District Council an Active Outdoor Gym\r
\r
INTRODUCTION\r
Tendring District Council has secured £65,000 of funding to develop an active outdoor gym on land adjacent to York Road Car Park in Holland on Sea.\r
\r
Objectives\r
The purpose of the gym will be to improve strength and balance through natural, every day movement, and to offer rehabilitation in those recovering from injury or illness. The equipment must reflect that the community groups most likely to use this will be those with poorer mobility/dexterity. The colours used for equipment should reflect the fact that there may be users with forms of dementia, for which some colours can prove challenging.\r
The gym may be utilised by groups undertaking rehabilitation with a trained professional, or by members of the public alone. The layout of the equipment should facilitate this.\r
The Council is seeking to enter a contract with a suitably qualified contractor to install new equipment that will meet the objectives allowing for the best use of the funds within the available space.\r
The successful contractor will design and build the gym, including the surfacing and access, project managing the process from start to completion, as well as providing the required warranties and maintenance information.

title: Asbestos Removal and Demolition of Carnavon House
description:
Demolition of Carnavon House and associated structures in Clacton on Sea.\r
\r
With reference to site plan and asbestos demolition report, demolish and \r
remove from site all arisings the building known as Carnavon House.\r
Structure to be removed 200mm below finish floor level. \r
Voids to ground level to be graded to adjacent levels with compacted type \r
1 aggregate. \r
\r
Asbestos to be removed by licensed contractor, appointed by principle \r
contractor. Principle contractor to include for all costs associated with \r
notification removal, air monitoring and proving client with relevant \r
certification upon completion . \r
\r
The site encompasses a 3 story building originally constructed c1960/70s. \r
The structure comprises of RC frame incorporating masonry infill. The \r
floors and roof are of concrete construction. \r
The building incorporates a lift and associated lift motor room to the room \r
and pit to the ground floor. \r
Internally the building includes lightweight partitioning. \r
The site also incorporates an external stair case and small storage areas. \r
The site is accessed from Carnavon Road to a small car park area. \r
Tendring discount council is currently in negotiations with UKPN for \r
the de energising of the electrical supply.\r
\r

      The project aims are to support ongoing work to improve engagement opportunities with the National Heritage List for England (NHLE) which is more commonly known as the List. In 2021-22, three pilot projects undertaken with external partners, such as civic or amenity societies, assessed the condition of the List in three selected areas.
       
      As well as helping us to improve our understanding of issues and limitations with the information contained within the List, this second phase of projects will help more people and communities connect with, and better understand, the extent and value of their local heritage. The work will help familiarise you and your team of volunteers with the regimes in place to help protect and promote this heritage, while giving you closer involvement with the designated heritage of your own area.

title: CA10968 - Life After Stroke Services
description:
Across England it is recognised that Stroke is the third largest cause of death, and a major cause of disability and social care need.  The impact of stroke is substantial, with high costs associated, long lengths of stay in hospital and high levels of avoidable disability and mortality. 

Within England:
•	Approximately 110,000 people experience a stroke every year.
•	20-30% people die within a month of experiencing a stroke.
•	25% of strokes occur to people under the age of 65.
•	There are approximately 900,000 people living with the effects of stroke.
•	300,000 people live with moderate to severe disability as a result of experiencing a stroke.
                                                                                        (National Stroke Strategy 2007)

Not registered:
